episodes.194744: Despite abnormally dry to drought conditions across central Indiana, following two weeks with no rain for most locations; dewpoints climbing to around 70 degrees on the 20th promoted scattered evening showers and thunderstorms with embedded isolated microbursts.||Synoptically, the broad subtropical upper ridge which had been suppressed south for much of the month, returned northward into the Midwest, with moderate south-southwesterly breezes increasing humidity and precipitable water values.  A boundary slowly crossing northwestern Indiana initiated convection.  Showers and storms with locally heavy downpours crossed the region, with damaging micobursts from the two strongest cells:  first late-day in south-central Howard County, and then later in the evening over south-central Marion County.
episodes.195289: A northward lifting warm front produced multicell clusters and scattered supercells across south and east central Minnesota. There were several reports of marginally severe hail and wind from the afternoon through the early evening.
episodes.195341: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 19th, as a cold front approached the area. Very strong instability combined with increasing deep layer shear to result in one of the thunderstorms evolving into a supercell. This storm was high-based with a deep layer of relatively dry air between the cloud base and the ground. This environment enabled the storm to produce very strong and damaging downbursts, which likely gusted to up to 95 mph at times. The storm moved across Pawnee Lake in Pawnee County, rolling multiple recreational vehicles at a campground. One person was killed when the RV he was in rolled, and two others were injured. This severe thunderstorm also produced large hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.195344: An isolated thunderstorm occurred during the evening of September 20th across Cherokee County Kansas.
episodes.195535: A microburst caused an approximately 10-mile swatch of damage through Kosciusko County. A second microburst resulted in a 6-mile swatch of damage.
episodes.195724: A cold front moved through north-central Minnesota in the late afternoon hours on Thursday, September 19, 2024. Out ahead of the cold front in northeast Minnesota, discrete severe thunderstorms began to form in far northeast Minnesota along the US Hwy 53 corridor around 4 PM CT. The first Severe Thunderstorm Warning was issued at 4:15 PM for parts of far northeast St. Louis County and northwest Lake County as the severe storm moved northeastward around 30 mph. By 4:55 PM, conditions within a different severe supercell thunderstorm warranted the first Tornado Warning of the evening to be issued for central St. Louis County around the communities of Cotton and Canyon, MN. Between 5 and 5:30 PM that evening, multiple additional Severe Thunderstorm and Tornado Warnings were issued along and east of US Hwy 53 and along the I-35 corridor into east- central Minnesota. The cold front continued to move eastward through the early evening hours on the 20th, with storms beginning to enter Douglas and Burnett Counties in northwest Wisconsin towards 6 PM as low-level funnel clouds were reported by law enforcement and trained weather spotters. Hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter was reported from the strongest thunderstorms, but in very localized reports. As the air mass began to cool and stabilized in the mid-evening hours, the threat for additional tornadoes began to wane and the strongest thunderstorms were limited to the Twin Ports and across northwest Wisconsin. As the cold front entered northwest Wisconsin by late evening, activity subsided to only showers and general thunderstorms with no additional impacts reported overnight. In total, eight Tornado Warnings, nine Severe Thunderstorms Warnings and two Special Marine Warnings were issued for this severe weather event.
episodes.195770: Storms developed along a boundary draped across northern Iowa on the afternoon of September 19th with additional storms through the evening on a cold front that moved across the area later in the evening. With over 2000 J/kg of available MLCAPE, steep lapse rates, and modestly curved hodographs that supported rotating updrafts, hail was reported in several of the storms that developed. Storms later into the evening produced wind damage in parts of southern Iowa.
episodes.195880: A passing upper level trough and surface Canadian cold front combined to result in a few showers and thunderstorms where the front stalled a bit across the Hi-Line. Winds along the front were already on the breezy side, so additional nudges from thunderstorms along the front were sufficient to result in gusts in excess of 58 mph.
episodes.195938: A short wave in the upper level flow pattern would position over the Central Plains region of the CONUS in tandem with an approaching cold front that would move into out of southern Missouri into northern Arkansas. A few severe thunderstorms would develop along the cold front across northern Arkansas with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.196063: A low pressure system moved across Colorado and int Kansas bringing a cluster of storms into far SW Kansas, tracking eastward along the Kansas/Oklahoma border.
episodes.196138: On September 19th, a lone severe thunderstorm developed a very impressive hail core aloft as it moved into Howard County. As it progressed through Howard County, it dropped quarter sized hail southeast of Riceville which damaged crops. Later into the evening, additional storms developed near the Mississippi River bringing isolated wind damage to Clayton County.
episodes.196551: Cold low pressure passing overhead helped trigger isolated thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. A couple of storms caused damage.
episodes.196664: The proximity of an upper level trough, along with an area of enhanced moisture, very light winds and strong heating resulted in explosive convection developing over Puerto Rico. The thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall, lightning, gusty winds, and even hail. Flooding and landslides were reported in several areas in Puerto Rico. Water surges along rivers were common, with some rivers even reaching flood stage.
episodes.196951: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of September 20th and quickly became severe as they entered into portions of central and south-central Kansas. Storms progressed eastward then produced up to quarter-sized hail and damaging wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph. However, some storms across south-central Kansas later into the evening and nighttime hours produced significant damage with wind gusts estimated to be up around 90 mph. Damage produced by these storms included high-profile vehicles and semis being blown over, a plethora of power poles and trees either damaged or snapped, and significant damage to a large outbuilding.
episodes.196972: A cold front triggered a broken line of strong thunderstorms south of the I-72 corridor during the late afternoon and early evening of September 20th.  One of the cells produced nickel-sized hail in Cumberland County.
episodes.196979: Thunderstorms n northeast wind flow erupted September 20, 2024, producing heavy rain, hail and snow at the end. There was also a large funnel cloud observed in the San Jacinto mountains west of Palm Desert. Minor flooding and debris flows occurred on the Line burn scar.

events.narrative: Strong thunderstorm wind overturned multiple recreational vehicles (RV) at a campground on the east shore of Pawnee Lake. Two people were injured and a man was killed when the RV they were in overturned.
Strong thunderstorm wind blew down numerous power poles and trees. Several roads had to be closed due to the significant amount of debris in the road.
Report from Mping.
Golf ball size hail damaged homes and vehicles.
Strong thunderstorm wind blew much of the roof off of an outbuilding.

Photos and video were received of large trees downed on several properties and on the roadway on Ham Lake Road in Danbury. One house also had a tree fall into the side of the house. Two properties along this road also had docks on Ham Lake that were damaged and flipped.
The public reported damage to a barn via social media east of Elkader. The barn had its door blown in and half of the roof blown off.
The public reported a corn field flattened along the east side of State Highway 52.
Hail to the size of quarters fell a few miles southeast of the town of Cherokee along the Cherokee and Crawford county line.
Delayed report. Two maple trees blown down. Damage to the top of an oak tree. Power lines damaged due to fallen trees.

Highway 127 was impassable due to being flooded with 1.5 feet of water plus rocks and debris. One car with four occupants was stuck and water was coming into the car.
Lightning set fire to a transformer.

A thunderstorms produced a series of microbursts along an approximately 10 mile path, starting just south of Leesburg and ending near the Whitley county line.  Numerous trees were broken or uprooted as well as many tree branches snapped. Multiple structures and power lines were impacted by the falling trees, causing pockets of damage, which centered on the Chapman Lake area. Winds were estimated in the 60 to 80 mph range, highest in the Chapman Lake area.
Mesonet station GW4063 Eagle Creek Colony measured a 55 kt gust.

The same storm what produced the microburst in Kosciusko County continued into Whitley County. Damage occurred from the Five Points area, southeast to State Route 205. Damage consisted of trees and intermittent structure damage in several non-continuous locations. Some crops were damage, especially near Riley Road.
An Ambinet station NE of Chester measured a 60 mph gust.
A landslide was reported in PR-119, Barrio Guacio, near a church. The road was impassable.
Hail was observed in the mountains between Lake Gregory and Twin Peaks. Videos of the hail on the highway was shared by Emergency Management while at the EOC.
Thunderstorm winds peeled back segment of older rubber cover on southern end of Taylor Elementary School's roof.
Mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 61 MPH.
A tree was blown down onto a powerline near the town of Mountain Home.
ASOS station KHVR Havre Airport measured a 54 kt gust.

Several photos and videos of a long lived extended funnel cloud moving north to south along the San Jacinto ridgeline, viewed from La Quinta. Convective showers and thunderstorms occurred over the mountains and a few moved into the valleys. Video showed clear rotation of the funnel.
ASOS station KHVR Havre Airport measured a 54 kt gust.
Mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 59 MPH.
A lightning strike hit the roof of a residence along PR-117, between km 9.8 and 10.4, in Barrio La Plata, Lajas.
